chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah from Humran who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Regarding the slaughtered animal of the Nāsib (those who bear enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt), the Jew, and the Christian, do not eat their slaughtered meat until you hear them mention the name of Allah.'
I said: 'And the Magian?' He said: 'Yes, when you hear him mention the name of Allah.'
Have you not heard the word of Allah: 'And do not eat from that upon which the name of Allah has not been mentioned'.

key_terms.النَّاصِب: Nāsib (one who bears enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for eating the meat of Jews, Christians, and Magians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that for the meat of the Nāsib (specifically in Shia context), Jews, Christians, and Magians to be permissible, one must hear them explicitly invoke Allah's name during slaughter, distinguishing this from mere general mention. It links this practical requirement directly to the Quranic prohibition of consuming meat upon which Allah's name was not mentioned, emphasizing the necessity of audible invocation for validity.
